chapter: Parade bands, instruments and the Eureka band
title: The record band, trumpet section and the scab band charge
summary: Gabriel describes the record band's trumpeters and why Clayton was not used, and how it was a scab band while he held a union card.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well, and I, I don't mean hip, one, I mean it's beat, just like I beat them, roll them down, yeah. Oh. I mean, the same thing up in there with them, but then I used to do that a long time, so I learned that from him. And another boy called Faiso, he went away from me, he beat that, he used to play a Louis Armstrong, he went away from me doing that too. Well, you know, this record band had them three trumpets, Poissy, T-Boy, and Tillman. And the trumpet players was regular in the band, and then sometimes they put Tillman on the sax when somebody don't come in, and that's the way that sax bass on, John Cashman played the clarinet.
When I first heard of you, Mika, they had Schatz. Well, yeah, we used Schatz in the band, but Schatz died, you know.

Yeah, Schatz was the trumpet player in the band, two Schatz, Schatz and T-Boy and Poissy. But then after when Schatz died, then they used Tillman. They never could use Clayton in the band because he couldn't read.
Yeah, he died, you know, a couple years ago.

Yeah, because, but we had, we would play, you know, any trumpet player could play, could read, they would hide, but they could not have to read. They would hide, but they could not use Clayton in the band, them kind of fellas.
Yeah, he didn't play in all the keys either, I don't think.

No, everything he played in the wrong key would start us up. And the record band done pretty good. There was a scab band, the record band, I'm going to tell you how it was. It was a scab band, and I belonged to the union, so they would be over at the Gypsy T-Room. When I would pass there, I had my boy playing clarinet in the band, and they wouldn't say nothing to me. I'd say, I'm teaching the band, and I'd get by with murder. Yeah. I'd pass there and I'd blow my clarinet all up in Williamson, fellas, they'd say, you know, man, it's crazy. Anybody else would do that, they'd charge him $50 a fine. Yeah. I played with another bunch of fellas from around here, a long time ago, let's see if I could come in with this bunch. I ain't never thought. Oh yeah, with the Sydney Fluesa, we had a band with Rudolph. The big Rudolph the drummer? Yeah, he played in the band Rudolph. I haven't seen him right now, I bet he's still here though. Yeah, I heard his clip of Rudolph, played a drummer, and his boy, Al Seed, played alto in the band, Al Seed. Sidney Fluesa played the banjo, and the boy they called T-Boy played bass from uptown, a little short fella called T-Boy.
